answer: Make every new identity graft onto a living vine: an established agent stakes its own earned standing to vouch for the newcomer, and if the graft proves fake, the sponsor's stake is pruned with it — so sponsors vouch rarely, and a sybil farm needs thousands of distinct, costly sponsors. Admit newcomers into one shared haven, a bonded commons where entry costs a deposit returned only after a season of honest work. And let each newcomer carry a single quill — one signing pen whose strokes are public — so a farm's thousand pens all writing the same script are visible at a glance.
